Hi Marco / Elena — thanks for flagging this. Quick summary up front: Marketplace consumption that AWS invoices is typically invoiced by AWS (AWS UK/Ireland entity for EU regions) and Redwood charges (e.g., Dedicated seat/Reserved Capacity) are invoiced by Redwood (Redwood Inc. or Redwood EMEA entity depending on contract). For VAT you can expect the following patterns: 

- AWS Marketplace line: billed by AWS (you should get an AWS VAT-compliant invoice; for reverse-charge the buyer (ACME) and AWS need the buyer VAT number on file). 
- Redwood invoice lines: billed by Redwood EMEA (if you contracted via our EU marketplace or a reseller flow) and will include our VAT registration if applicable.

To resolve this I'll loop in finance (Marcus) and channel/marketplace (Karthik) and legal (Vanessa). Rafael — quick finance note:

- The Reserved Capacity invoice in this case was issued by Redwood EMEA Ltd (Ireland), VAT IE12345678. I’ve attached a copy of our VAT certificate to the internal thread (redwood_vat_cert_emea.pdf).
- For marketplace-line items: AWS issues those invoices and we don’t appear on that invoice as the seller if the purchase was routed through AWS Marketplace standard flow. In that scenario, ACME should receive an AWS invoice showing the AWS VAT registration and your VAT number should be added to that AWS billing profile for reverse-charge posting.
- W-8BEN-E vs W-9: those forms apply when a US payer is making payments to a foreign payee and for US tax withholding. Since ACME is an EU buyer and the marketplace charge is handled by AWS EU entity, the W-8/W-9 is not required from ACME for that specific marketplace line. Redwood may require a W-8BEN-E if the buyer is a non-US entity and payments flow through a US Redwood entity — but for EMEA invoicing this is typically not the case.

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.inference.com>

Subject: Re: Invoice shows AWS marketplace & Redwood - VAT treatment?

A few legal/tax clarifications: 

- EU reverse-charge: If ACME is VAT-registered in Italy and the supply is a B2B service supplied by an EU supplier, typically the reverse-charge applies and the buyer self-accounts the VAT. That requires the buyer VAT number to appear on the invoice and the supplier to be VAT-registered. If AWS issued the marketplace invoice, ACME must ensure their VAT number is captured in AWS Marketplace buyer profile.
- Marketplace models vary: (1) AWS acts as the vendor-of-record (VoR) and issues the invoice (VoR flow), (2) Redwood is the VoR and AWS facilitates payment (direct vendor flow), or (3) a reseller/partner (third-party) issues invoices. The tax outcome changes with that model.
- W-8/W-9: These are US forms. W-8BEN-E is for non-US entities receiving payments from US payers; W-9 is for US entities receiving payments. You (ACME) do not need to submit W-8/W-9 to Redwood if Redwood is invoicing via Redwood EMEA Ltd. However, if any part of the deal is routed through Redwood US (rare for EU customer), our payments team may request W-8.

Suggested language to send ACME: we should confirm their billing legal entity and VAT number, request they add it to their AWS Marketplace profile, and indicate Redwood can supply our VAT registration evidence on request. For expedited handling, we can also provide a short supplier certificate and a DocuSign addendum that authorizes AWS to reissue with the buyer VAT on file.

I’ll review any templates before we send to ACME.

-Vanessa
VP, Legal | Redwood Inference
